questions.stem: When must the continuous listening watch begin?
options: 15 minutes before the vessel is underway
When the lines are cast off
When the first call is received
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 252(1) starts the watch 15 minutes before the vessel is underway.

questions.stem: The watch may end when the vessel is:
options: anywhere out of sight of land
securely anchored, moored or made fast, and in a place where she is not a hazard to passing vessels
questions.explanation: Both conditions in s. 252(1)(a) and (b) must be met.

questions.stem: A vessel is outside a BC traffic zone. Which channel is the listening watch kept on?
questions.explanation: Schedule 4 item 2(a): Channel 16 outside a traffic zone.

questions.stem: Inside a traffic zone the watch channel is:
options: the appropriate VHF channel for that zone
questions.explanation: Schedule 4 item 2(b) names the appropriate VHF channel, the one in Notices to Mariners or law for vessel traffic management.

questions.stem: What does 'appropriate VHF channel' mean in NSR 2020 Part 2?
options: The channel specified in Notices to Mariners or law for vessel traffic management in a traffic zone

questions.stem: What must be true of the radio during the watch?
options: It must be set to low power
It must be on Channel 70 only
It must be off during manoeuvres
It must operate with sufficient gain to permit an effective continuous listening watch
questions.explanation: Section 252(2) requires sufficient gain; a turned-down radio does not meet the rule.

questions.stem: When may the continuous watch be interrupted?
options: Whenever the master is on deck
For short periods while the only VHF is used on another channel
questions.explanation: Section 252(3): where there is no additional VHF installation the watch may be interrupted for short periods.

questions.stem: A tug is anchored in a narrow tideway. The master thinks she may be a hazard to passing ships. What does MPR s. 254 require?
options: The watch may stop because she is anchored
The master ensures a continuous listening watch is maintained
Only the engine room must be manned
A navigation safety call every hour
questions.explanation: MPR s. 254 requires the master of an anchored or moored vessel to keep the watch if, in the master's opinion, she may be a hazard to passing vessels.

questions.stem: A person keeping the watch who is not in charge of the deck watch hears something that affects safe navigation. They must:
options: tell the person in charge of the deck watch without delay
write it down and report at handover
ignore it unless it is a mayday
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 250(2) requires them to inform the person in charge without delay.

questions.stem: What are the call signs of the BC MCTS centres?
questions.explanation: RAMN Part 2: Victoria MCTS is VAK, Prince Rupert MCTS is VAJ. Both are open 24 hours and English only.

questions.stem: A vessel with a NAVTEX receiver must also:
options: keep a continuous watch on the maritime safety information frequencies appropriate to time, position and equipment
questions.explanation: Section 248 covers VHF, MF, MF/HF, NAVTEX and similar equipment.
